---
title: "Integrating Randomisation into National Legislation"
---

## Overview

For a Managing Authority to use randomisation as part of its beneficiary selection process, the legal framework governing that programme must either explicitly permit it or be flexible enough to accommodate it without ambiguity. Most national frameworks were designed around two conventional selection methods — ranking proposals by score, or first-come-first-served — and say nothing about random assignment. A clear legal basis is the precondition for experimental evaluation to happen at all.
DG Regio provided formal confirmation that randomisation is permissible under EU Cohesion Policy rules. The key regulatory anchor is Article 44 of the Common Provisions Regulation (EU) 2021/1060, which requires Managing Authorities to evaluate the effectiveness of their programmes but does not prescribe the method — creating space for RCTs as the most rigorous option available.
